facts.title: Long Walk to Freedom — author
facts.text: Long Walk to Freedom was written by Nelson Mandela.

facts.title: Apartheid — South Africa historic policy
facts.text: Apartheid was a racial-segregation policy in South Africa; F.W. de Klerk was the country’s last white president.

facts.title: ANC — South Africa and Mandela
facts.text: The African National Congress is a South African political organization, and Nelson Mandela joined it in 1944; this is historic political context.

facts.title: East London — South Africa location
facts.text: East London is a city in South Africa.

facts.title: Desmond Tutu — Anglican cleric
facts.text: Desmond Tutu was an Anglican cleric and anti-apartheid leader.

facts.title: Mandela — imprisonment period
facts.text: Nelson Mandela was imprisoned from 1964 until his release in 1990.

facts.title: Rainbow Nation — source sobriquet
facts.text: The source uses Rainbow Nation as a sobriquet for South Africa; it is retained as source-attributed language rather than a formal designation.

facts.title: Egypt — 1952 monarchy and 1953 republic
facts.text: Egypt’s monarchy ended in 1952, and the republic was proclaimed in 1953; the source’s compressed wording is not reproduced.

facts.title: Tahrir Square — Cairo
facts.text: Tahrir Square is in Cairo, Egypt.

facts.title: Alexandria and Port Said — Egyptian ports
facts.text: Alexandria and Port Said are Egyptian Mediterranean port cities.

facts.title: Valley of the Kings — Egypt location
facts.text: The Valley of the Kings is in Egypt.

facts.title: United Arab Republic — 1958 formation
facts.text: Egypt and Syria formed the United Arab Republic on 1 February 1958; this is a bounded historic political-union reference.

facts.title: Mohamed Naguib — first Egyptian president
facts.text: Mohamed Naguib was Egypt’s first president after the republic was proclaimed; this is historic office context.

facts.title: Suez Canal — construction and inauguration
facts.text: Work on the modern Suez Canal began in 1859, and the canal was inaugurated in 1869.

facts.title: Suez Canal — Mediterranean and Red seas
facts.text: The Suez Canal connects the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea.

facts.title: Suez Canal — 1956 nationalization
facts.text: Gamal Abdel Nasser nationalized the Suez Canal Company in 1956; this is historic political-economic context.

facts.title: Suez Canal — 1967 closure and 1975 reopening
facts.text: The Suez Canal closed after the 1967 war and reopened for international navigation in June 1975.

facts.title: Cleopatra VII — Ptolemaic dynasty
facts.text: Cleopatra VII was a daughter of Ptolemy XII and the last queen of the Ptolemaic dynasty in Egypt.

facts.title: Hassan al-Banna — Muslim Brotherhood founder
facts.text: Hassan al-Banna founded the Muslim Brotherhood in Egypt in 1928; this is historical political-organizational context.

facts.title: Gamal Abdel Nasser — historic presidency
facts.text: Gamal Abdel Nasser was president of Egypt from 1956 until 1970; the record is historic-office context only.

facts.title: Anwar Sadat — Nobel Peace Prize
facts.text: Anwar Sadat and Menachem Begin jointly received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1978.

facts.title: Hosni Mubarak — historic presidency
facts.text: Hosni Mubarak was president of Egypt from 1981 until February 2011, when he stepped down amid popular unrest.

facts.title: Mohamed Morsi — historic presidency and death
facts.text: Mohamed Morsi was president of Egypt from 2012 to 2013 and died in 2019 after collapsing in court; this is historic political and legal context.

facts.title: Freedom and Justice Party — Morsi candidacy
facts.text: The Freedom and Justice Party selected Mohamed Morsi as its candidate in Egypt’s 2012 presidential election.

notes.title: South Africa MCQ quality boundary
notes.text: Questions with essentializing group labels or an unbounded white-rule duration premise are excluded. Accepted questions have readable stems, four options, and a visually confirmed printed key.

notes.title: Egypt reference source-error boundary
notes.text: The source’s British-colony wording, compressed transition chronology, rankings, intelligence-agency line, and unsupported superlatives are excluded. Political facts are historically scoped.

notes.title: Suez and Cleopatra source boundary
notes.text: Canal chronology and Cleopatra’s dynasty fact are retained only with corroboration. Popular epithets and the source’s Ptolemaic naming generalization are not imported as neutral facts.

notes.title: Egypt political-biography boundary
notes.text: Historical office and organization facts are retained with neutral scope. Rhetorical, causal, ideological, conflict-framing, and first-Muslim-Nobel wording are excluded.

notes.title: Egypt MCQ source-key boundary
notes.text: The Morsi-party question is excluded because its printed key conflicts with the Freedom and Justice Party evidence. Cleopatra-epithet, colonial-status, and Muslim-Brotherhood-as-party questions are also withheld.

mcqs.question: লং ওয়াক টু ফ্রিডম গ্রন্থের রচয়িতা—
নেলসন ম্যান্ডেলার রাজনৈতিক দলের নাম কী?
Long Walk to Freedom গ্রন্থটির লেখক কে?
আফ্রিকান ন্যাশনাল কংগ্রেস যে দেশের রাজনৈতিক দল?
কোন দেশকে রেইনবো নেশন বলা হয়?
মুসলিম ব্রাদারহুড কোন সালে প্রতিষ্ঠিত হয়?
নিম্নের কোন দেশটি ভূমধ্যসাগরের তীরে অবস্থিত?
আনোয়ার সাদাত কোন দেশের প্রেসিডেন্ট ছিলেন?
মিসর ও সিরিয়া কত সালে একত্রিত হয়ে ইউনাইটেড আরব রিপাবলিক গঠন করেছিল?
মিসরে রাজতন্ত্রের অবসান ঘটে কবে?
